hints: Work backwards from the hydroxynitrile, remember HCN only adds across a C=O bond in an aldehyde or ketone.
Draw out 2-hydroxybutanenitrile as $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CN}$ and remove HCN to reveal the carbonyl compound.
Ask yourself which type of alcohol oxidises to that aldehyde with mild oxidation, primary to aldehyde or secondary to ketone.
walkthrough:
**Work Backwards From the Cyanohydrin**

Think like a detective and start at the end. HCN adds to aldehydes and ketones to make hydroxynitriles (cyanohydrins).

$$\text{aldehyde/ketone} + \text{HCN} \rightarrow \text{hydroxynitrile}$$

**Identify the Carbonyl Compound**

2-hydroxybutanenitrile is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CN}$. The carbon bearing OH and CN was the $\text{C=O}$ carbon.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO} + \text{HCN} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CN}$$
So the oxidation product must be propanal, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$.

**Link Aldehyde Back to Alcohol Y**

Now recall mild oxidation rules. Primary alcohols oxidise to aldehydes, secondary alcohols oxidise to ketones.

$$\text{primary alcohol} \xrightarrow{[O]} \text{aldehyde}$$
To get propanal (3 carbons, aldehyde), Y must be the 3-carbon primary alcohol, propan-1-ol.

options.A: Butan-1-ol is a primary alcohol so it oxidises to butanal, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$. That would add HCN to give 2-hydroxypentanenitrile (5 carbons), not the 4-carbon product required.
options.B: Butan-2-ol is a secondary alcohol so it oxidises to the ketone butanone, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$. HCN addition to a ketone would give 2-hydroxy-2-methylbutanenitrile, with two alkyl groups on C-2, not 2-hydroxybutanenitrile.
options.C: Propan-1-ol is a primary alcohol and is mildly oxidised to propanal, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$. Propanal then undergoes nucleophilic addition with HCN to give exactly $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CN}$, 2-hydroxybutanenitrile.
options.D: Propan-2-ol is a secondary alcohol so it oxidises to propanone, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$. HCN addition would give 2-hydroxy-2-methylpropanenitrile, $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C(OH)CN}$, which is branched and incorrect.
